reader.requirement: At --std 85, when DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA is in effect (written in the program or inherited by a contained program), NUMVAL must interpret a comma in argument-1 as the decimal point in both formats (leading sign, or trailing sign/CR/DB), for literals and alphanumeric items; a period in that case violates the rule and the result is undefined (A.2.2).

reader.notes: The renderer passes commaMode from the compilation unit's (possibly inherited) DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA to the one NumvalDec scanner; no edition test sits on the path. Both formats, items, ref-modified items and a contained program read the comma as the decimal point at --std 85.

refuter.evidence: rnv1b.cob (DPC): NUMVAL(ND(2:2)) of PIC 9(4) 1234 ->23; NUMVAL(group ' 2,5')->2,5; NUMVAL(TE(K)) subscripted '1,234 '->1,234; IF NUMVAL("1,5") > 1,4 -> GT; ' 0,000000000000000001 ' -> 0 at 4 places; ' -,5 '->-0,5; '5,  DB'->-5; 2*NUMVAL("1,25")+0,5 -> 3; and a SEPARATELY compiled second program in the same source without DPC reads '3.75' as 3.7500 (the comma mode does not leak across compilation units). cite.py: OK §1989:A.2.29.3 AR3; OK §1989:A.2.29.3 AR1. LEAD FOR AR1 (rule 1989-AR-A.2.29.3-1, not this case): rnv1.cob NUMVAL(NE) on a PIC -ZZ9,99 numeric-edited item is refused, COBOL1627 'EDITED category ... CATEGORY wording of ISO §2023:15.67.3 r1'. At 1985 numeric edited is class alphanumeric (OK §1985:IV.4.3.3) and the Alphanumeric argument type is 'A data item of the class alphabetic or alphanumeric' (OK §1989:A.2.2, its item 3), Table 1 typing NUMVAL X1; AR1's 'alphanumeric data item' is read as CATEGORY by IntrinsicArgumentRules NUMVAL row (CharacterCategory Since 85). That is a class-vs-category reading for AR1's own refuter; AR3's comma rule holds for every argument the compiler admits.
